title: When a joint venture or general partnership interest is a security
rule: An investment contract, and so a security, is an investment of money in a common enterprise with profits to come solely from others' efforts. In the Fifth Circuit, which covers Texas, a general partnership or joint venture interest ordinarily is not one, because partners hold real control, unless the agreement leaves the partner little more power than a limited partner, the partner is too inexperienced to use its powers, or it cannot replace a manager whose unique skill it depends on.

citation.authority: SEC v. W.J. Howey Co., 328 U.S. 293 (1946); Williamson v. Tucker, 645 F.2d 404 (5th Cir. 1981)
